notes: Four-post LinkedIn series with selected winning positions, a trough-to-date return window and a one-year-only composite return planted, and a net-and-gross 1/5/10 standardized block and a testimonial carrying client, compensation and conflict disclosures as decoys.

planted.span: Three positions we added to our Small Cap Value portfolios in the spring of 2025, a short-line railroad operator, a specialty coatings manufacturer and a dental consumables distributor, have returned 64%, 51% and 47% through June 30, 2026.
planted.explanation: Returns of three hand-picked winning positions are shown without providing, or offering to provide, the performance of the Small Cap Value portfolios they were extracted from.

planted.span: Measured from the October 12, 2022 market low through June 30, 2026, our Dividend Growth composite has returned 58.6% net of fees.
planted.explanation: The headline window is chosen to start at a market trough to inflate the result; the standardized periods that follow do not cure a start date selected for its favorable outcome.

planted.span: Our Balanced Income composite, which we have managed since 2009, returned 9.8% net of fees (10.6% gross) for the twelve months ended June 30, 2026.
planted.explanation: Performance of a composite with more than ten years of history is shown for the one-year period only, with no five- or ten-year results.

decoys.span: Standardized performance for the composite, periods ended June 30, 2026 (five- and ten-year figures annualized): 1 year 11.2% net / 12.1% gross; 5 years 9.6% net / 10.5% gross; 10 years 10.4% net / 11.3% gross.
decoys.why_ok: Each gross figure sits beside a net figure of equal prominence for the same period, and the one-, five- and ten-year periods are all shown.

decoys.span: You explained every change before you made it, and in nine years I have never once felt rushed into a decision.
decoys.why_ok: The testimonial is accompanied by clear disclosure that the writer is a current client, was not paid or given anything of value, and has a material conflict because her son works at the firm.
